description: Japanese EX Battle Boost card import.
method: This import contains 99 numbered card records: 001–093/093 plus six secret numbers 094–099/093. No unnumbered card entries were found in the independent checklists or cited scans.

Official Japanese card detail pages provide the 93 base records. The official catalog returned 97 records total: it omits secret cards 094–095 and exposes 096–099 as image-less detail records whose number field is not the printed number. Independent checklists and the cited card scans verify the actual printed numbers 096/093–099/093; the scans also verify 094/093–095/093.

The Japanese collector checklist states 99 total cards (93 main-set cards and six secret cards) and lists all six secret numbers. Serebii checklist scans for 094–099 were checked for card identity and printed numbering. The records for 094 and 095 reuse matching official gameplay data from EBB-020 and EBB-043, respectively.

Card variants are recorded per printed card number in this manifest and each card file. The independent itemized collector catalog distinguishes first-edition, unlimited, and reverse-holo entries; its per-card item list is the variant crosswalk. #044 Zekrom EX is holo only with first-edition and unlimited forms, consistent with card-level foil listings and its distinction from mirror #043.

The official detail pages for #097–099 state those cards are included in first-edition-marked packages; the cited scans show the first-edition mark. This import therefore records their normal and reverse-holo first-edition forms only and omits unlimited forms, despite broader catalog listings. #096 has no such official restriction and retains both editions as listed.
All EBB cards preserve the official no-rarity-symbol value. No marketplace IDs or unverified artwork URLs are added.
